a: A rough email pattern is .+@.+\..+ but real validation is stricter.
\d{10,15} matches a run of 10 to 15 digits.
\b marks a word boundary between word and non-word chars.
cat|dog matches either cat or dog.
\. matches a literal dot, not any character.
Flag m makes ^ and $ match line starts/ends.
Flag i ignores case when matching.
Most languages offer a regex replace for substitutions.
